# Answerlore

> Answerlore loads the service manuals a company already owns, answers technician questions in
> plain language with the manual page attached, and says "not in the knowledge base" instead of
> guessing.

Answerlore is a cited answer layer for multi-brand field service. It is built for independent
service companies and equipment dealers whose technicians work across many manufacturers'
equipment and cannot memorize all of it.

Last updated: 2026-09-21

## What it does

- Ingests service manuals, bulletins, and internal notes into topic-scoped documents, one topic
  per document, each carrying the source file, the page range, the revision, and the date a
  human last verified it.
- Answers a question with a short answer, the steps if there are steps, and a citation naming
  the document, the section, the manual revision, and the page number. Answers are short by
  default, under 200 words, because the technician is standing at the equipment.
- Refuses when no loaded document settles the question, names the team to ask, and logs the
  question as a documentation gap with a count of how often it is asked.
- Drafts a customer-safe version of the answer with part numbers, root causes, and internal
  escalation paths removed, for a technician to review and send.

## What it is not

- Not a ticket deflection bot. A human still handles the ticket.
- Not a vector database product. Retrieval is search over structured files, and a support lead
  corrects a wrong answer by editing the source document.
- Not self-serve. Access starts with a guided trial, then a Knowledge Map engagement.
- Not SOC 2 certified. Single-tenant by construction; see the Your data page.

## Who it is for

Independent authorized service agencies and equipment dealers, typically 8 to 75 people, whose
technicians service equipment from several manufacturers. Users are field technicians,
dispatchers, service managers, and inside sales representatives.

## Pricing

Flat monthly price per company, not per seat. Starter $750 per month billed annually,
Standard $1,500, Scale $3,000, each with a one-time Knowledge Map and ingestion fee of $3,500
to $7,500. A 30-day founding-customer pilot is $750. Every figure, both billing rates, and the
tier limits: https://answerlore.com/pricing.md

## Key pages

- [How it works](https://answerlore.com/how-it-works): ingestion, retrieval, citation, refusal,
  and the honest list of what it does not do.
- [Why it refuses](https://answerlore.com/why-it-refuses): the design argument for refusing to
  guess, with the sources for the claims.
- [Pricing](https://answerlore.com/pricing): three tiers, both billing rates, the Knowledge Map
  fee, the pilot, and what the first year costs.
- [Your data](https://answerlore.com/your-data): where manuals live, who can see them, and what
  certifications the company does and does not hold.
- [A worked Knowledge Map](https://answerlore.com/knowledge-map-example): a complete ticket
  map for a fictional dealer, arithmetic shown.
- [Resources](https://answerlore.com/resources): published guides. First guide:
  [Fifteen Working Days a Year, on Hold](https://answerlore.com/hold-time), what a call to a
  manufacturer's tech support line costs a service company.
- [About](https://answerlore.com/about): who builds Answerlore and how to correct a page.
